title: RematchRequested v1
description: Published by the Matching Service's rematch sweeper, which periodically (REMATCH_INTERVAL, default 2 min) re-queues requests that are waiting for a resource: UNMATCHED requests (a resource may have appeared since) and requests still PENDING after REMATCH_PENDING_AGE (their RequestCreated event was lost, e.g. the Request Service crashed between storing and publishing). Exchange emergency.events (topic, durable), routing key request.rematch.<type in lower case>, persistent, content type application/json, AMQP message-id = eventId. It goes to the same queue as RequestCreated (matching.request-created, also bound with request.rematch.*), and the consumer treats it the same way: re-read the request, match it only if it is still PENDING or UNMATCHED. So a duplicate or stale message never claims twice. It carries only the request's ID and type, not the request: the consumer reads the current request from storage anyway.

reason.description: UNMATCHED: no resource was found earlier; one may exist now. STALE_PENDING: the request has stayed PENDING longer than REMATCH_PENDING_AGE, so its RequestCreated event was probably never delivered.
